newsitem.title: USA: Endocardial says FDA clears atrium trials.
newsitem.headline: Endocardial says FDA clears atrium trials.

text.p: Endocardial Solutions Inc said the U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved the use of the company's EnSite 3000 System and EnSite catheter in the right atrium in a multi-center clinical study.

"This approval, coupled with our recently announced approval for ventricular clinical trials, keeps us on track to file our application for premarket allowance (PMA) in late 1997 or early 1998," said chief executive Jim Bullock.

Endocardial's cardiac diagnostic system provides a 3-D graphical display of the heart's electrical activity. It is designed to help physicians rapidly and accurately diagnose abnormally rapid heartbeats in cardiac patients who cannot be fully evaluated using existing techniques.

The company said last month that it had asked the FDA for permission to use its system in trials involving the right atrium of the heart. Trials using the system in the left ventricle of the heart were previously approved, it said.
The company went public in March.
